introduction: Taqíyyih, concealing or denying one’s faith under threat, was permitted and even praised in Shí‘ih Islam. The Báb’s and Bahá’u’lláh’s writings at certain moments told believers to practise concealment for their safety; Bahá’u’lláh says of Himself that He “is not capable of dissimulation”; and present Bahá’í law forbids denying one’s faith, though it does not require proclaiming it. The guide sets these side by side. Scripture is similarly divided. The Qur’an praises the believer of Pharaoh’s house “who hid his faith” and excuses one “forced thereto”; Naaman is told “Go in peace”; Esther hides her people; Joseph of Arimathaea is a disciple “secretly”. Against them stand Daniel’s open windows, the three who would not bow, and Jesus’s “whosoever shall deny me”, with Peter weeping after his denial.
questions: What is the difference between not announcing one’s faith and denying it? Where do the readings draw the line, and where does Jesus?
Naaman is told “Go in peace”. Daniel opens his windows. What would you want to know about a situation before saying which example applies?
Why might a religion permit concealment in one period and forbid it in another?

outside.why: “This Wronged One is not capable of dissimulation.” Daniel, when the decree was signed, prayed with his windows open, as he did aforetime.
The reading quotes this verse: a believing man of Pharaoh’s family, who hid his faith, said: would ye kill a man because he saith: my Lord is Allah?
Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear, besought Pilate that he might take away the body.
A youth of twenty imprisoned for announcing his belief. Be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods.
This year all are commanded to practise concealment. Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
All forbidden to confess the Cause before men. See thou say nothing to any man.
Observe dissimulation while imprisoned. Naaman the Syrian, newly a believer, asked pardon in advance for bowing beside his master in the house of Rimmon; and Elisha said, Go in peace.
The Shí‘ih tradition: no faith for one without dissimulation. Its Qur’anic ground: save him who is forced thereto and whose heart is still content with the Faith.
In teaching, wisdom is required. Neither cast ye your pearls before swine.

If we deny the Cause we may be able to remain at home. Jesus leaves no room: whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven. Peter denied and was forgiven. How do readings 5 to 9 and reading 13 divide the ground between concealing one’s faith and denying it?
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
To deny that one is a Bahá’í while believing is dissimulation, and Bahá’í law does not allow it. With the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew it. Later he told her the time for silence was over. What changes between a time for concealment and a time when it becomes a betrayal?
